title: Radial transfer estimates and polygon length laws for honeycomb walks
main_claim: For critical honeycomb polygons modulo translation (weight x_*^L, x_*=(2+sqrt2)^{-1/2}): A(r)=r^{-2+o(1)}, P(r)=r^{-2/3+o(1)}, M_2(r)<=r^{2/3+o(1)}. As a consequence, the length tails are n^{-3/2} and n^{-1/2}, and D=n^{3/4+o(1)} in probability under length cutoffs.

issues.location: sections/plateau.tex, angular.tex, radial.tex, two-04..two-08 (one-mark ratio N^{-2/3} and two-mark k^{-4/3} analytic core)
issues.description: The Hilbert–Schmidt link and coercivity arguments behind Prop. one-mark-ratio and Thm two-mark are written too compactly to check line by line, so the analytic core rests on compressed claims. This is a reviewer note about verifiability, not a located error.
issues.evidence: For example, the plateau link construction asserts that the HS bounds are 'locally uniform' and that the discrepancy costs at most C D^{-2} times squared-cell sums, with only a sketch. The exponent bookkeeping around these steps checks.

coverage: Read intro, tails.tex, two-10 cutoff consequences, the end of pressures.tex (Press-5..Press-8 and the thin-cylinder span proposition) and the start of plateau.tex. Verified by hand all the exponent bookkeeping in Cor. length-cutoffs: the bin split at n^{3/4}; the reverse bound F(n)>=n^{-3/2-5δ/2}; the conditional ratios n^{-2ε}, n^{-2ε/3}, R^{-ε} and R^{-ε/2}. Verified the tail conversion: the lower bounds from collision diameter >= N|h|; the upper bound via three orientations with N=R^{1-ε} and the tall-contractible suppression; and the length-weighted loss identity (Fatou plus domination, with E_N->0). Checked the thin-cylinder span proof: the connected-subgraph signed sum equals ±T_G(1,0), whose magnitude is >=1; the star bound gives sum w(1+H)^{m-1}<=C N^{m-2} from M_γ>=(H-2)A_N≈c(H-2)/N; the contractible-to-winding splice face geometry R_ij,P_{i+1,j},R_{i+1,j},P_{i+1,j+1},R_{i,j+1},P_{i,j+1} is a valid hexagon with single-path overlaps; the averaging gives partner mass >=A_N/N. Checked the cap injection and the strip stacking argument. Did not re-derive the deep spectral/radial analysis; I relied on the sibling board entry, which records numerical checks of the constants (c_*=2-sqrt2, 7/12, 9/8, 5/24, etc.).
sibling_notes: The board already had a rank-160 entry for this dir with no_gap_found and extensive constant checks. This re-audit agrees with it and adds checks of the cutoff, tail-conversion and thin-cylinder steps. Companion papers in family 237 (bridge mass, marked polygons, signed cylinders) report the same exponent system (5/24, 9/8, -4/3, 3/4), consistent with this paper.
